card: Splits the monolithic test_IsStandard unit test into independent test cases for each policy rule in src/test/transaction_tests.cpp. It replaces mutable global variables like g_dust and g_bare_multi with an explicit StandardPolicy struct and constructs fresh transaction fixtures declaratively for each check to eliminate cross-test state leakage. This is an internal test cleanup supporting issue #36692, with no changes to node validation or mempool policy logic.
changed_since_previous: Added declarative transaction construction for each check, introduced a `CheckDustThreshold` helper to deduplicate threshold boundary assertions, and added an explicit length check for the 42-byte OP_RETURN script.
evidence: Part of #36692 ('Declarative construction of test data'): 'This splits it into one test case per policy rule, each building its own transaction... so no case changes policy for another' (PR description).
problem: Tests for transaction standardness rules previously mutated a single shared transaction object iteratively across disparate checks while relying on mutable global fee and policy variables. This coupled checks together, risked test-state leakage between assertions, and made failures harder to trace.

risk.why: Changes are entirely restricted to unit test fixtures, so mistakes would only cause test failures rather than node bugs.

summary: Splits the monolithic `test_IsStandard` unit test in `src/test/transaction_tests.cpp` into independent test cases for each mempool policy rule. Replaces mutable static globals (`g_dust`, `g_bare_multi`) with an explicit `StandardPolicy` struct passed to test helpers, and switches to declarative per-check transaction construction using new `MakeTx` and `CheckDustThreshold` helpers.
